questions.text:
2-bromobutane exists as enantiomers (optical isomers).

CH3-CH2-CHBr-CH3

Draw the enantiomers of 2-bromobutane in the box below.
questions.expectedAnswer: Two 3D structural drawings of 2-bromobutane showing the four different groups (CH3, CH2CH3, H, Br) arranged around the chiral C2 as non-superimposable mirror images of one another.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises tetrahedral arrangement and identifies asymmetric C.

questions.text: Explain why 2-bromobutane can exist as enantiomers.
questions.expectedAnswer: 2-bromobutane has a chiral centre (asymmetric / stereocentre carbon) at C2, which is bonded to four different groups (-CH3, -CH2CH3, -H, -Br). This means the molecule and its mirror image are non-superimposable — they are enantiomers.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies asymmetric C. Merit: Draws TWO correct 3D structures AND explains.

questions.text:
Devise a reaction scheme to convert 2-bromobutane into butanamide.

CH3-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-NH2   (butanamide)

For each step include:
- the reagents
- the structural formula of the organic product after each step.
questions.expectedAnswer: Step 1: 2-bromobutane + KOH(alc)/heat -> but-1-ene (elimination, Hofmann minor product). Step 2: but-1-ene + H2O/H+ (or HBr then OH-) via anti-Markovnikov route to give butan-1-ol. Step 3: butan-1-ol + Cr2O72-/H+ with heat and excess oxidising agent -> butanoic acid (oxidation). Step 4: butanoic acid + SOCl2 -> butanoyl chloride. Step 5: butanoyl chloride + concentrated NH3 -> butanamide.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE correct conversion. Merit: THREE correct conversions. Excellence: Complete scheme.

questions.text:
Polylactic acid (PLA) is a polyester used in dissolvable surgical sutures. It is made from lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid):

HO-CH(CH3)-COOH

Draw a section of the PLA chain to show THREE repeating units.
questions.expectedAnswer: Three repeating units showing: -[O-CH(CH3)-C(=O)]3- with ester linkages formed between the -OH and -COOH groups of adjacent lactic acid monomers (each unit carries a -CH3 branch on the carbon between the ester oxygens).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws polymer with ester linkages. Merit: Correctly draws THREE repeating units.

questions.text: Identify and explain the type of reaction occurring to form PLA.
questions.expectedAnswer: Condensation polymerisation. An ester bond is formed between the -OH and -COOH groups of adjacent monomers, with loss of a water molecule each time.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies condensation. Merit: Explains with ester bond and loss of water.

questions.text:
Below is the structural formula of a dipeptide:

H2N-CH(CH2OH)-CO-NH-CH(CH2SH)-COOH

Circle the amide (peptide) linkage on the dipeptide above.
questions.expectedAnswer: Circle the -CO-NH- group (the amide/peptide bond) linking the two amino acid residues.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly circles amide linkage.

questions.text:
The dipeptide can undergo a chemical reaction to form the following products (zwitterion forms of the two amino acids).

Identify and justify the type of chemical reaction that has occurred.
questions.expectedAnswer: Acidic hydrolysis has occurred. Water has been used to split the amide (peptide) linkage, regenerating the two amino acids.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises hydrolysis. Merit: Explains the process.

questions.text: Draw the structural formulae of the organic products formed when the dipeptide is heated under reflux with sodium hydroxide solution.
questions.expectedAnswer: Two products: the sodium salts of the two amino acids (with -COO-Na+ instead of -COOH).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws two organic products. Merit: Shows -COO- instead of -COOH.

questions.text:
Complete the table below to show the structural formula or the IUPAC name for each compound.

Compound A: IUPAC name = methyl pentanoate
Compound B: structural formula = CH3-CH2-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-CH3
Compound C: structural formula = CH3-CH(Cl)-C(=O)-H
Compound D: IUPAC name = 4-hydroxyhexanoyl chloride
questions.expectedAnswer: A (methyl pentanoate): CH3-O-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH3. B (CH3CH2C(=O)CH2CH2CH3): hexan-3-one. C (CH3-CH(Cl)-C(=O)H): 2-chloropropanal. D (4-hydroxyhexanoyl chloride): Cl-C(=O)-CH2-CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: THREE correct. Merit: ALL correct.

questions.text: Draw THREE constitutional (structural) isomers of Compound C that contain a carbonyl group (C=O).
questions.expectedAnswer: Three structural isomers containing a carbonyl group with the same molecular formula.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: TWO correct. Merit: ALL correct.

questions.text:
Complete the flowchart by drawing structural formulae for Compounds A, B, C, D, and E, and identifying Reagents 1, 2, 3, and 4.

Starting material: butan-2-ol (CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3)
-> conc. H2SO4, heat -> Compound A
Compound A + H2O/H+ -> Compound B
Compound A + Reagent 2 -> Compound D
Compound D + Reagent 3 -> CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-NH2
CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-NH2 + H2SO4(aq) -> Compound E
Compound B + Reagent 1 -> Compound C
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound A: but-2-ene (from elimination of butan-2-ol with conc. H2SO4 and heat). Compound B: butan-2-ol (addition of H2O to but-2-ene, Markovnikov). Compound C: butan-2-one (oxidation of the secondary alcohol butan-2-ol with acidified dichromate — Reagent 1 = Cr2O72-/H+). Compound D: 1-bromobutane or 2-bromobutane formed by addition of HBr to but-2-ene (Reagent 2 = HBr). Reagent 3 = excess NH3 in ethanol (substitution to give butan-1-amine). Compound E: butan-1-aminium hydrogensulfate (salt from CH3CH2CH2CH2NH2 + H2SO4).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: FIVE correct entries. Merit: SEVEN correct. Excellence: ALL correct.

questions.text:
Six organic compounds are given in a table.

1: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH2OH
2: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-C(=O)H
3: H2C=CH-CH2-CH2-C(=O)H
4: CH3-CH=CH-C(=O)(Cl)
5: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-C(=O)(Cl)
6: H2C=CH-C(=O)-CH2-CH3

Choose the appropriate organic compounds to match observations from chemical tests.

- Heating with acidified potassium dichromate causes orange to green change. Heating with Tollens' reagent does not produce a silver mirror.
- Heating with Fehling's reagent forms an orange-red solid. Mixing with potassium permanganate causes purple to decolourise and a brown solid to form.
- Mixing with water results in steamy fumes, and bromine water changes from orange to colourless.
questions.expectedAnswer: Test 1: Compound 1 (primary alcohol). Test 2: Compound 3 (aldehyde + alkene). Test 3: Compound 4 (acyl chloride + alkene).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: THREE correct compounds. Merit: FOUR observations linked to functional groups. Excellence: ALL linked with reaction types.

questions.text:
Justify your chosen structural formula for each of the three compounds.

Relate the observations to functional groups and reaction types.
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound 1: primary alcohol oxidised by dichromate. Compound 3: aldehyde reduces Fehling's, alkene decolourises KMnO4. Compound 4: acyl chloride reacts with water producing steamy fumes.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: THREE reaction types. Merit: FOUR observations linked to functional groups. Excellence: ALL linked.

questions.text:
A student prepared a pure sample of ethyl methanoate in the laboratory:

Step 1: Add methanoic acid, ethanol, and concentrated H2SO4.
Step 2: Heat under reflux for 30 minutes.
Step 3: Add sodium carbonate until bubbling stops.
Step 4: Add water and separate layers.
Step 5: Add drying agent.
Step 6: Distil the organic layer.

Describe the function of the concentrated H2SO4 in step 1.
questions.expectedAnswer: The concentrated H2SO4 acts as a catalyst/dehydrating agent.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies the role.

questions.text: Give TWO reasons to explain why the reaction mixture was heated under reflux in step 2.
questions.expectedAnswer: (1) Heating increases the rate of reaction. (2) Reflux prevents loss of volatile reactants/products.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: ONE reason. Merit: TWO reasons.

questions.text: Why was sodium carbonate added in step 3?
questions.expectedAnswer: Sodium carbonate neutralises the concentrated H2SO4 and any remaining methanoic acid.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies neutralisation.

questions.text:
Explain how distillation was used in step 6 to purify the ethyl methanoate from the organic layer.

Refer to relevant boiling points:
Methanoic acid: 101 degrees C
Ethanol: 78.4 degrees C
Ethyl methanoate: 54.3 degrees C
questions.expectedAnswer: The mixture is heated carefully in a distillation apparatus. Ethyl methanoate has the lowest boiling point (54.3 degrees C), so it vaporises first and is condensed and collected, leaving behind the higher-boiling ethanol (78.4 degrees C) and methanoic acid (101 degrees C). Collect the fraction at approximately 53-56 degrees C.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises boiling point determines separation. Merit: References boiling points. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
Consider Compounds A, B, and C:

Compound A: CH3-CH(Cl)-CHO
Compound B: CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-NH2
Compound C: H2N-CH2-CH2-CHO

Choose the ONE compound that has ALL the following properties:
- cannot exist as enantiomers
- forms a silver mirror when heated with Tollens' reagent
- turns damp red litmus paper blue.

Explain your choice.
questions.expectedAnswer: Compound C (H2N-CH2-CH2-CHO, 3-aminopropanal). It does not exist as enantiomers because none of its carbons are bonded to four different groups (no chiral centre). It has an aldehyde (-CHO) group, so it forms a silver mirror when warmed with Tollens' reagent. It has a primary amine (-NH2), which is a weak base, so it turns damp red litmus blue. Compound A is eliminated because it has a chiral carbon (C2 bonded to Cl, CHO, H, CH3) and no amine group. Compound B is eliminated because it has a chiral carbon and no aldehyde (no silver mirror).
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Chooses correct compound. Merit: Explains choice with TWO properties. Excellence: Full explanation with all three properties.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional isomer of C5H9ClO that has the following properties:
- exists as enantiomers (optical isomers)
- branched carbon chain
- produces steamy fumes upon addition of water.
questions.expectedAnswer: 2-methylbutanoyl chloride, CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-C(=O)Cl. This has a branched carbon chain (methyl branch on C2), an acyl chloride group (C(=O)Cl) which produces steamy fumes of HCl when water is added, and a chiral centre at C2 (bonded to CH3, CH2CH3, H, and COCl), so it exists as a pair of enantiomers. Formula C5H9ClO.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws a branched chain or acyl halide. Merit: Correct structural formula.

questions.text:
Draw the structural formula for the constitutional isomer of C5H9OBr that has the following properties:
- exists as cis-trans (geometric) isomers
- straight chain arrangement
- causes a colour change of orange to green when heated with acidified potassium dichromate to produce an organic product that does not react with Benedict's solution.
questions.expectedAnswer: An example is 1-bromopent-3-en-2-ol: BrCH2-CH(OH)-CH=CH-CH3. Formula C5H9BrO. It is a straight chain, has a C=C double bond with two different groups on each sp2 carbon (so it shows cis-trans isomerism), and the -OH is on a secondary carbon (C2), so acidified dichromate oxidises it to a ketone (1-bromopent-3-en-2-one). Ketones do not react with Benedict's reagent, matching the observation. Orange to green colour change confirms the oxidation by dichromate.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Draws a C=C bond or secondary alcohol. Merit: Correct formula for one part. Excellence: Correct formulae for both (ii) and (iii).
